_: THE COMPOSITION CONTRACT. A Study page is vertically scrollable, so height is not a scarce resource and the resolver does not try to fit a composition into the visible rectangle. Layout selection is WIDTH-DRIVEN. Height grows and the page scrolls.
order: 1  content semantics       — the composition family, authored, never inferred
2  intrinsic demands       — what each region and each figure actually needs, measured at layout time
3  choose the composition  — a NAMED state from that family's ladder
4  allocate width          — to the chosen state, computed from scratch
5  let height grow         — height:auto, no target page height

_  The order this replaces was: take the available rectangle, divide it, shrink things to fit, and reject when the two sides do not occupy similar heights. That is fitting rectangles, not composing a lesson.

origins._: PERMANENT HORIZONTAL ORIGINS. Every region lands on a named origin; nothing is positioned because it happens to be narrower than the space around it, and nothing is ever centred. The build measures each region's left edge and fails if it is not on its declared origin.
origins.content: the teaching surface's left inset — where a title, a question, a figure, a synthesis and a stacked solution all begin
origins.secondaryTrack: the second track of a two-track state — where a split solution or an interpretation rail begins
origins.figure: the same as `content`: a plane is left-aligned in its region in every state
origins.readingEnd: origin + the region's reading measure. A ceiling, not a width to fill

whitespace._: NOT EVERY UNUSED PIXEL IS A DEFECT. Treating them alike is what made the last resolver stack a pair to avoid 94px and thereby create 766px.
whitespace.readingMargin: DESIRABLE. A 608px prose column on a 1152px page does not become 1152px wide.
whitespace.structural: DESIRABLE. Space below the shorter side of a legitimate two-track row is hierarchy, not a hole.
whitespace.unowned: DEFECTIVE. A 720px region containing a 390px plane because the region inherited an allocation.
whitespace.invariant: No child is stretched, distorted or arbitrarily positioned to consume unused space. Unused page width may remain as page margin. Unused width INSIDE a composition region must arise from an explicit region measure or an alignment rule.

figure._: A FIGURE IS MEASURED BEFORE ANY TEXT TRACK IS ALLOCATED. Leftover width is never a figure size. The signature is in SCALE — px per authored unit — because what makes a plane legible is a scale, not a box.
ladder: 1  preferred scale + gap + interpretation.min fits            -> side, at the preferred scale
2  else, if shrinkPolicy allows: the largest scale in [minimum .. preferred] that still leaves interpretation.min -> side
3  else                                                       -> stack, and RECOMPUTE the figure against the whole content region
figure._shrinkNote: MAINTAINER RULING STILL OPEN, but now it is a named policy rather than a buried comparison. `allow` lets a plane reduce within its own legal range before the side state is abandoned; `hold` makes it keep its preferred scale and stack instead.

instructionSplit.purpose: a balanced worked example: a question with real content beside a solution with real content

instructionFlow.purpose: A LEGITIMATE PRESENTATION TYPE, NOT A FALLBACK. A short task, a rule, then the reasoning at a controlled reading width, growing downwards. Most worked examples are this shape: the question is one line and the solution is the lesson.

repeat._: Judged on each complete item's minimum width, never on height. Children share one verdict.

visualInterpretation._: NO HEIGHT TEST. A 700px plane beside a 180px explanation is a good relationship: the plane is the object being explained and the prose does not have to fill its height. The previous global occupancy gate was semantically wrong here and rejected exactly that.

stack.purpose: regions in semantic order on the content origin

ladders._: EXPLICIT STATE TRANSITIONS. There is no generic fallback that keeps reallocating width until something fits — that is where unpredictability came from. Each rejected candidate DISCARDS ALL OF ITS COMPUTED DIMENSIONS and the next state is measured from scratch.
extended: per state, from the ladder its own content needs

height._: HEIGHT DOES NOT PARTICIPATE IN LAYOUT SELECTION, with exactly one exception.
height.policy: height:auto; the page scrolls; there is no target page height in Study mode
height.exception: instructionSplit's promptSubstance test — the shorter track's content height as a fraction of the row. It is the one signal that a question is not a track, and it SELECTS A DIFFERENT PRIMITIVE (instructionFlow) rather than rejecting the content.
height.viewportBound: Focus mode and the workbook workspace are viewport-bound and are out of scope here.
